notes: Fixtures are small Python 3.9 projects (standard library, unittest) under evals/fixtures/. Each run copies one into a scratch directory and runs `git init` + one commit there, so the diff against the untouched fixture can be graded — never inside this repository. Every case runs twice, non-interactive: with the skill (the sub-agent reads SKILL.md as if loaded by the skill tool) and without_skill as baseline. Cases run one at a time with the user's go-ahead before the next. grade_mechanical.py checks the mechanical assertions (tests, removed test lines, host growth, function length, abstract types); the rest is graded by reading the diff and final_reply.md. Its 'abstract types with < 2 implementations' check counts nominal subclasses only, so a Protocol always shows 0 — verify Protocols by hand. Full scenarios and results: code-design-workflow-test.md.

evals.name: god-class
evals.fixture: evals/fixtures/shop — OrderService (173 lines) mixing validation, pricing, persistence, mail, reporting
evals.prompt: /code-design Add discount codes to order placement: a customer can enter one code when placing an order. Codes are either a percentage (e.g. 10%) or a fixed amount (e.g. 5 EUR), each has an expiry date, and each customer can redeem a given code only once. Codes are applied after the loyalty discount and before shipping and tax are calculated.
evals.expected_output: Discount rules and redemption tracking in their own units; OrderService only delegates; discount logic tested directly; no single-implementation abstraction; design notes with principle and rejected alternative.
assertions: All tests pass (existing and new)
No test removed or altered in pre-existing test files (import-line edits allowed)
Discount rules (percentage, fixed, expiry) live in a production module other than shop/service.py
OrderService holds no discount rule or redemption rule itself — it only calls into discount units
Redemption tracking (once per customer) is held outside OrderService
Discount logic is tested without constructing OrderService
No ABC/Protocol with fewer than two implementations
place_order — the function the change extends — is at most 30 lines afterwards
Existing paths moved out of place_order are covered by tests that existed or were written before the move (vacuously true if nothing was moved)
Final reply contains a design-notes table with principle and rejected alternative per decision

evals.name: third-exporter
evals.fixture: evals/fixtures/reports — CSV and HTML exporters with copy-pasted money/date formatting and totals, both tested
evals.prompt: /code-design Add a Markdown export for the monthly sales report, the same columns and totals as the CSV and HTML exports.
evals.expected_output: The duplicated formatting and totals are extracted once and used by all three exporters (rule of three reached, covered by tests); the Markdown exporter does not copy the logic a third time.
assertions: All tests pass (existing and new)
No test removed or altered in pre-existing test files (import-line edits allowed)
The money formatting (German format, thousands separator) exists exactly once in production code
Month filtering, cancellation filter, sorting, and totals/by-region aggregation exist exactly once in production code
csv_export and html_export use the extracted shared code (not only the new Markdown exporter)
CSV and HTML output is byte-identical to before (existing exact-match tests unchanged and green)
The Markdown exporter has its own test(s) with an exact or row-level expected output
No exporter registry, factory, or plug-in mechanism, and no abstraction with fewer than two implementations (YAGNI)
Final reply contains a design-notes table with principle and rejected alternative per decision

evals.name: kiss-guard
evals.fixture: evals/fixtures/textkit — a small module of pure text helper functions
evals.prompt: /code-design Add a function that turns article titles into URL slugs: lowercase, ASCII only (transliterate umlauts), words joined by hyphens, at most 60 characters without cutting a word.
evals.expected_output: A plain function in the existing helper module, with tests; no class, interface, factory, or configuration object; design notes record 'extend existing module' with its reason.
assertions: All tests pass (existing and new)
No test removed or altered in pre-existing test files (import-line edits allowed)
The slug function is a plain module-level function in textkit/text_utils.py (no new module)
No new class, ABC/Protocol, factory, registry, or configuration object is introduced
Umlauts are transliterated (ä->ae, ö->oe, ü->ue, ß->ss) and tested
The 60-character limit without cutting a word is tested
Existing helpers are reused where they fit (normalize_whitespace / strip_accents) instead of reimplemented
The diff touches no existing function except where reuse requires it
Final reply contains a design-notes table that records the extend-existing-module decision with its reason

evals.name: seam
evals.fixture: evals/fixtures/pricing — price calculation as pure domain logic, no I/O
evals.prompt: /code-design Prices must be shown in the customer's currency. Convert using live exchange rates from https://rates.example.com/latest?base=EUR (JSON: {"rates": {"USD": 1.08, ...}}).
evals.expected_output: A domain-named abstraction for exchange rates owned by the pricing side; the HTTP call only in an adapter; tests use a fake and never reach the network; conversion logic unaware of HTTP.
assertions: All tests pass (existing and new) without network access
No test removed or altered in pre-existing test files (import-line edits allowed)
The HTTP call (urllib/http client, the URL) appears in exactly one adapter unit and nowhere in prices.py or display.py
Conversion and display logic depend on a domain-named abstraction or a passed-in rate/function, not on the HTTP adapter
Tests replace the rate source with a fake/stub; no test patches urllib or the network module
The adapter's JSON parsing is tested with a canned response (no network)
gross_price and VAT/volume rules remain unchanged and EUR-based
No abstraction beyond the one seam (no factory, registry, or second interface without a second implementation or test double)
The adapter has a timeout and a defined failure behaviour, and the rate fetch does not run once per price line (fetched once and passed, or cached)
Final reply contains a design-notes table with principle and rejected alternative per decision
